source_read: PMC HTML full text PMC9926328 (title confirmed; Key Points, Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results with the Table, Discussion, Limitations, Conclusions read in full). Figures 1 to 4 are images: a screenshot of Figure 3 came back blank (figure image not viewable). Online supplements (eTables 1 and 2, eFigure, protocol) not read.

claims.overstatement: No material overstatement; the claim follows the Table rather than the abstract and keeps 'associated with' and the attribution caveats. Small wording points: (1) the statement's 'Peak ratings on 0-100 scales' are peak changes from each session's baseline (the magnitude says so correctly); (2) 'without knowing which brownie they had eaten' rests on the double-blind design, and the paper reports no check of blinding; (3) 'divided-attention error' is the mean distance of the cursor from the moving target (higher is worse; units not printed); (4) the magnitude's 'printed Cohen's d values for the effects do not match the printed means and SDs' is true of several but not all (drug effect 0.5, memory 0.3, routine tasks 0.6 and the THC and 11-OH-THC Cmax and AUC values agree with a pooled-SD calculation). No dosing or potentiation guidance: doses appear as study conditions.
claims.note: All numbers in statement and magnitude found as printed. Editors' arithmetic recomputed: THC Cmax 14.8/8.2 = 1.80, AUC 84.9/33.3 = 2.55; 11-OH-THC Cmax 53.9/4.5 = 11.98, AUC 349.0/34.0 = 10.26; same as the claim (about 1.8, 2.5, 12, 10). Every pair the claim calls significant carries the Table's c marker (Tukey P < .05 between active conditions); anxious, paranoid, sleepy, pleasant and liking carry no c marker. The text prints dry or red eyes after the CBD-dominant extract as 28.7, the Table 28.8. Peak-time values are means of individual peak times; their ranges never exceed 6.0 h although assessments ran to 24 h; no test of peak time is reported. Duration of the stronger effects: only in Figures 3 and 4, which were not viewable, so the claim's 'not given in the parts that could be read' stands.

anchors.extracted: Inclusion: age 18 to 50, BMI 18 to 34, past experience with cannabis, no cannabis use in the 30 days before the first session, negative urine drug tests at screening and at every session, healthy by blood tests, history and examination; recruited by media advertisements and word of mouth.
36 signed consent, 22 randomized, 18 completed (11 men, 7 women); mean age 30 (SD 7) years; mean 124 (SD 80) days since last self-reported cannabis use, median 93, range 39 to 295.

anchors.locator: Methods › Study Design and Procedures, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Within-participant double-blind crossover, January 2021 to March 2022, Johns Hopkins Behavioral Pharmacology Research Unit; three 14-hour outpatient sessions: placebo brownie (ethanol vehicle), THC-dominant extract brownie (20 mg THC, no CBD), CBD-dominant extract brownie (20 mg THC + 640 mg CBD), study conditions; order by randomized Latin square; at least 1 week between sessions; dropouts replaced; pharmacist prepared and dispensed drugs to keep staff and participants blind; 30 minutes after the brownie a CYP probe cocktail (caffeine 100 mg, omeprazole 20 mg, losartan 25 mg, dextromethorphan 30 mg, midazolam 2 mg) in all 3 sessions; serial assessments for 24 h after the cocktail.

anchors.locator: Methods › Cannabis Extracts and Study Drugs, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Two whole-plant extracts from the NIDA Drug Supply Program: THC-dominant 70% THC, 2.7% CBG, 1.5% CBN, under 1% THCV, CBC and delta-8-THC, no detectable CBD; CBD-dominant 59.3% CBD, 2.1% CBC, 2.0% THC, 1.1% CBG, under 1% CBN, THCV and delta-8-THC. The two conditions therefore also differ in minor cannabinoids, not only in CBD.

Drug Effect Questionnaire items on a 100 mm visual analogue scale (0 not at all to 100 extremely), ratings and vital signs at baseline and 0.25 to 24 h after the cocktail, tasks at baseline and 0.5 to 24 h; tasks: digit symbol substitution (total correct), modified paced serial addition (total correct), divided attention (mean distance of cursor from a moving central box); heart rate seated, automated monitor.

CBD-dominant vs THC-dominant extract, mean (SD), n = 18, paired t tests, units not printed with the values: THC Cmax 14.8 (5.5) vs 8.2 (4.0); 11-OH-THC Cmax 53.9 (22.6) vs 4.5 (1.9); THC-COOH Cmax 118.6 (44.8) vs 45.1 (18.5); THC AUC 84.9 (29.38) vs 33.3 (16.9); 11-OH-THC AUC 349.0 (137.1) vs 34.0 (16.4); THC-COOH AUC 1030.0 (456.4) vs 445.7 (196.2); all P < .001. Editors' ratios 1.80, 2.55, 11.98, 10.26.

No significant effect of time in the placebo-brownie session (cocktail alone changed no PD outcome). CBD-dominant vs THC-dominant: feel drug effect 72.8 (25.9) vs 59.2 (31.1), P < .001; pleasant no difference between active conditions; unpleasant 38.6 vs 19.6, P = .015; sick 26.1 vs 11.6, P = .013; red or irritated eyes 28.7 vs 15.9, P = .037; trouble with memory 37.8 vs 27.4, P = .03; difficulty with routine tasks 46.7 vs 30.3, P = .02.

anchors.locator: Table (Mean Peak Change From Baseline Values), rows Drug effect to Difficulty performing routine tasks; footnotes b and c
anchors.extracted: Peak change from baseline, mean (SD), placebo / THC-dominant / CBD-dominant, n = 18: drug effect 9.4 / 59.2 / 72.8 (b,c); unpleasant 4.1 / 19.6 / 38.6 (b,c); sick 3.4 / 11.6 / 26.1 (b,c); dry or red eyes 3.6 / 15.9 / 28.8 (b,c); memory impairment 5.6 / 27.4 / 37.8 (b,c); routine tasks 6.6 / 30.3 / 46.7 (b,c); anxious 4.1 / 13.3 / 23.9 (CBD-dominant b only); paranoid -0.1 / 12.0 / 23.4 (b, no c); sleepy -12.9 / 21.0 / 42.6 (b, no c); pleasant 12.0 / 55.9 / 57.9 and liking 23.8 / 52.6 / 60.6 (b, no c). Peak time of drug effect 2.1 h (range 0 to 4.0) THC-dominant vs 2.9 h (0.5 to 6.0) CBD-dominant; no test reported. c = Tukey P < .05 between the active conditions.

anchors.locator: Results, 4th paragraph; Table, Cognitive and Physiological measures rows
anchors.extracted: CBD-dominant vs THC-dominant: paced serial addition -22.7 (24.6) vs -6.6 (19.1) correct, P = .049; divided attention distance 32.7 (39.2) vs 15.9 (24.7), P = .04; digit symbol not significantly different between active conditions (-9.9 vs -2.7); heart rate +25.4 (20.9) vs +10.1 (14.1) beats/min, P = .001; no effects on blood pressure.

anchors.locator: Abstract › Results and Conclusions and Relevance; Key Points › Findings
anchors.extracted: Authors conclude the CBD-dominant extract gave stronger adverse effects, which contradicts common claims that CBD attenuates THC's adverse effects, and that CBD inhibition of THC and 11-OH-THC metabolism is the likely mechanism (no mediation analysis). The abstract also says anxiety and sedation rose compared with both THC alone and placebo, which the Table does not show for THC alone (no c marker).

Primary aim was cannabinoid-drug interactions with the five probe drugs (losartan AUC the primary outcome); probe-drug pharmacokinetics are left to later papers. Limitations: one dose of THC and of CBD, no CBD-only condition, outcomes measured with the probe cocktail which may have contributed to the behavioural effects, not powered for sex differences.

key_findings.correction: Values are peak changes from baseline (Table title), not peak ratings; the numbers are right. Red eyes is 28.8 in the Table, 28.7 in the text.

Locator: Methods › Cannabis Extracts and Study Drugs, 1st paragraph. Editors' arithmetic rechecked (20/0.02 = 1.0 g and 640/0.593 = 1.08 g of extract; CBC 21 to 23 mg, CBG 11 to 12 mg; about 29 mg of THC-dominant extract).

reporting_issues.note: Table b markers after the THC-dominant extract: unpleasant, paranoid, sleepy, irritable, heart racing, throat irritation and dry mouth; text says only dry mouth.

Rechecked by pooled-SD calculation. Two further mismatches in the contrasts the claim uses: dry or red eyes CBD-dominant vs THC-dominant printed d 1.0 (about 0.4 from the printed means and SDs) and paced serial addition printed -0.5 (about -0.7). Intervals including zero next to P < .05 also for memory (0.3, -0.6 to 1.2, P = .03), routine tasks (0.6, -0.4 to 1.5, P = .02), PASAT, DAT and heart rate against THC alone.
640/0.593 = 1079 mg extract, 21.6 mg THC at 2.0%; 20 mg THC needs 1000 mg extract with 593 mg CBD.

risk_of_bias.note: RoB 2 overall some concerns agreed. In the measurement domain, 'self-ratings were made blind to condition' rests on the double-blind procedure; the paper reports no check of blinding, which does not change the judgment because the two active brownies carried the same nominal THC dose.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: the abstract's anxiety and sedation statement against THC alone is not supported by the Table, and the mechanism is asserted without a mediation analysis while probe-drug levels are unreported.

missed: Peak-time ranges in the Table never exceed 6.0 h although measures ran to 24 h; how long the stronger effects lasted is shown only in Figures 3 and 4 (not viewable here), so the card cannot state duration.

The many printed d intervals that include zero beside P < .05 (memory, routine tasks, PASAT, DAT, heart rate against THC alone) suggest the intervals ignore the within-person design; cite P values and means, as the card advises.
